items.t: Enel stock: Nine-month profit rises as dividend outlook holds
sum: Enel reported stronger nine-month results on November 12, as growth in Spain and the Americas more than offset weaker margins in Italy. The company also confirmed its 2026 outlook and approved an interim dividend.

According to the Enel Group's results release, revenue for the first nine months rose 8.9 percent to 65,022 million euros. Ordinary EBITDA increased 4.0 percent to 17,946 million euros, while group net ordinary income rose 6 percent to 6,018 million euros.

Enel said the performance of its grid businesses in Spain and Latin America was the main growth driver. Lower average prices for residential and small-business customers in Italy, along with reduced hydro generation caused by lower water availability, weighed on margins.

The board approved an interim dividend of 0.245 euros per share, payable from January 20, 2027. Enel also confirmed its 2026 forecast for ordinary EBITDA of between 23.1 billion and 23.6 billion euros and group net ordinary income of between 7.1 billion and 7.3 billion euros.

On November 9, Enel and Leonardo signed a memorandum of understanding covering potential cooperation in energy products, sustainable mobility, security, digitalization and satellite communications. The Enel Group announcement said the companies intend to explore solutions for energy flexibility, infrastructure security and industrial competitiveness.
Enel stock traded at 9.92 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:24 CET on Saturday, November 14.

Enel stock in focus after nine-month profit rises 6%
sum: Enel reported stronger results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, while warning that weaker Italian margins remain a constraint. In its nine-month results release published on Thursday, November 12, Enel said growth in Spain and the Americas more than offset lower profitability in Italy.

Enel stock traded at 9.89 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:42 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026, 0.40 percent below the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The comparison uses the 9.93-euro Xetra close from the prior session.

Revenue rose 8.9 percent year over year to 65.022 billion euros from 59.702 billion euros. Ordinary EBITDA increased 4.0 percent to 17.946 billion euros, while group net ordinary income advanced 5.5 percent to 6.018 billion euros. Reported net income, which includes non-ordinary items, reached 5.634 billion euros, up 7.6 percent.

Enel said distribution activities in Latin America benefited from tariff adjustments, while Spain gained from a new regulatory framework. Renewable generation, particularly in Colombia, and higher wholesale electricity sales in Europe also supported revenue. Enel Grids produced ordinary EBITDA of 7.295 billion euros, up 11.7 percent from the year-earlier period.

Italy remained weaker. Lower average prices for residential customers and small and medium-sized businesses reduced sales margins, while lower water availability weighed on hydropower generation. Ordinary EBITDA from the integrated businesses declined slightly to 10.772 billion euros as the group continued to reduce exposure to commodity volatility.

Capital expenditure increased 19.1 percent to 8.140 billion euros. Enel Grids accounted for 5.431 billion euros, or 67 percent of the total, while Enel Green Power received 1.660 billion euros. Including acquisitions, total investment reached 9.049 billion euros, supported by a US solar portfolio and assets in Spain and Italy.

That expansion came with higher leverage. Net financial debt stood at 66.158 billion euros at September 30, compared with 57.182 billion euros at the end of 2025. The net debt-to-equity ratio rose to 1.32 from 1.22. Investors therefore face a trade-off between the group's regulated-network growth and the financing burden of its investment plan.

Enel Americas stock: Q3 EBITDA jumps 38% as guidance holds
sum: Enel Américas delivered a stronger third quarter, with EBITDA rising 38% year over year and net income increasing 86%. The results were discussed at the company’s third-quarter and nine-month conference call on October 30, 2026, and reported by Investing.com on November 1.

Reported EBITDA reached 1.42 billion US dollars in the quarter, supported by stronger generation in Colombia, solid grid performance and favorable currency movements in the Colombian peso and Brazilian real. Colombia accounted for 54% of quarterly EBITDA, while Brazil contributed 39%.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 20% year over year to 1.239 billion US dollars, before a 179 million US dollar foreign-exchange benefit lifted reported EBITDA. Net income reached 390 million US dollars, while cash from operations rose 15% to 880 million US dollars.

For the first nine months of 2026, adjusted EBITDA increased 14% year over year to 3.425 billion US dollars. Reported EBITDA rose 24% to 3.845 billion US dollars, including a 420 million US dollar foreign-exchange benefit. Management confirmed its full-year 2026 EBITDA and net income guidance, saying performance remained in line with expectations.

The company also highlighted a 5% share buyback completed during the quarter and an interim dividend equivalent to 15% of net income as of September, payable in January 2027. Investment reached 1.6 billion US dollars in the first nine months, with grid spending increasing as Enel Américas continued to strengthen and digitalize its distribution networks.

Enel Américas generates and distributes electricity across Colombia, Brazil, Argentina, Central America and Peru. Its business combines an integrated generation portfolio with electricity grids serving 23.2 million customers, according to management. In Colombia, the company said its solar fleet was the country’s largest, with 985 megawatts of installed capacity after the Atlántico project entered commercial operation.

Enel stock gains as Leonardo partnership targets energy security
sum: Enel and Leonardo signed a memorandum of understanding on November 10, 2026, covering cooperation on energy, security and digital technologies, according to Decode39. The companies are exploring joint solutions for energy products, sustainable mobility, critical-infrastructure protection, digitalization and satellite communications.

Enel CEO Flavio Cattaneo and Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani signed the memorandum. The proposed cooperation could support energy-management systems, industrial sustainability, self-generation and monitoring applications based on satellite technology. The companies also identified potential programs of national strategic importance.

The arrangement brings Enel's energy and infrastructure capabilities together with Leonardo's expertise in cybersecurity, digital systems and satellite communications. For Enel, the commercial opportunity lies in developing value-added services for industrial customers rather than in an immediate change to its regulated utility operations.

The memorandum is not a binding contract for specific projects. The companies said subsequent agreements could define individual transactions, subject to applicable rules and related-party requirements. Investors therefore still need evidence of contracts, investment commitments and financial contributions before assigning a material earnings effect to the initiative.

Enel stock traded at 9.90 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:43 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 0.41 percent above the Xetra close of Monday, November 9, at 9.86 euros. The move places the share above the previous Xetra session's close as the market weighs the new cooperation against the group's broader investment program.
Italy's broader market context remains relevant for investors following Enel stock through the FTSE MIB.

For Enel, the next material test is whether the partnership develops into binding commercial projects with measurable revenue or investment implications. More news and analyses on Enel stock will follow the company's operating and strategic updates.

There May Be Underlying Issues With The Quality Of Enel Chile's (SNSE:ENELCHILE) Earnings
sum: Enel Chile S.A.'s (SNSE:ENELCHILE) robust earnings report didn't manage to move the market for its stock. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

Importantly, our data indicates that Enel Chile's profit received a boost of US$238m in unusual items, over the last year. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. Which is hardly surprising, given the name. We can see that Enel Chile's positive unusual items were quite significant relative to its profit in the year to September 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items are making its statutory profit significantly stronger than it would otherwise be.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

As previously mentioned, Enel Chile's large boost from unusual items won't be there indefinitely, so its statutory earnings are probably a poor guide to its underlying profitability. For this reason, we think that Enel Chile's statutory profits may be a bad guide to its underlying earnings power, and might give investors an overly positive impression of the company. But the happy news is that, while acknowledging we have to look beyond the statutory numbers, those numbers are still improving, with EPS growing at a very high rate over the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. So if you'd like to dive deeper into this stock, it's crucial to consider any risks it's facing. Every company has risks, and we've spotted 4 warning signs for Enel Chile (of which 1 is significant!) you should know about.
This note has only looked at a single factor that sheds light on the nature of Enel Chile's profit. But there is always more to discover if you are capable of focussing your mind on minutiae.

items.t: Enel stock gets new grid signal from Colombia infrastructure plan
sum: Enel is adding a new grid-infrastructure angle to its investment case after a regional plan in Colombia outlined more than 30 electricity projects. The initiative expands the focus beyond the Chile battery pipeline discussed in the previous report.

The Bogotá-Región 2030 plan covers substations, high-voltage lines and medium-voltage networks across Bogotá and Cundinamarca. According to La Republica, 14 projects are already operating, two are under construction and the remaining initiatives are moving through studies and environmental licensing.

The operating projects have lifted installed capacity in Bogotá and Cundinamarca from 3,510 MVA to 4,860 MVA, according to the same report. Projects under construction include the Intexzona and Guaymaral substations, which are planned to add 246 MVA to the regional transmission system.

The plan offers visibility on network investment and regional power demand, but projects still in studies or licensing have a longer route to operation. The report does not provide a direct earnings contribution for the individual projects, so the near-term financial impact remains tied to execution and the group's broader results.

Enel stock gains as Chile battery pipeline reaches 600 MW
sum: Enel stock traded at 9.48 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:31 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 1.72 percent above the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 3. The move comes as Enel's Chilean subsidiary advances four battery energy storage systems with a combined capacity of 600 megawatts.

Argus Media reported on October 29 that construction remains on track, citing Enel Chile chief executive Gianluca Palumbo during a results conference call. The projects will operate alongside existing solar and wind plants and use grid-forming technology, which helps maintain voltage and frequency as renewable generation takes a larger role in the power system.

The first project to begin operations is the 205-megawatt Las Salinas battery. It has recently connected to the grid and is expected to start commercial operations in 2027. The project would be Chile's first battery installation using grid-forming technology, according to Argus Media.

The 153-megawatt Valle del Sol and 94-megawatt Azabache projects are also scheduled to start in 2027. Construction of the 100-megawatt Finis Terrae project began in August, with commissioning planned for 2028. Once all four facilities are complete, Enel Chile's battery storage capacity in the country is expected to reach 800 megawatts.

For Enel, the projects extend the strategic role of storage beyond adding generation capacity. Grid-forming batteries can provide system support traditionally associated with conventional power plants, potentially helping renewable assets operate in a more stable network. The projects also give the group a visible pipeline in a market where regulation is encouraging the integration of grid-forming capability into battery, solar and wind facilities.

The storage update was accompanied by stronger operating figures at Enel Chile. January-to-September profit rose 11 percent year on year to 390 million US dollars, while hydro generation increased 3 percent to 8.2 terawatt-hours after heavier rainfall from August. Enel Chile is the country's largest generator, with installed capacity of 8.9 gigawatts.
The earnings improvement does not remove the wider risks for the group.

Enel stock faces results test as Endesa regulated earnings gain weight
sum: Enel stock faces its next earnings test after subsidiary Endesa reported stronger nine-month results on October 28. The update adds a more detailed read-through on earnings quality before Enel presents its group figures on November 12.

Endesa's official results release said net profit rose 15 percent to EUR 1.962 billion and ordinary net profit increased 22 percent to EUR 2.125 billion. EBITDA advanced 8.4 percent to EUR 4.577 billion, allowing the subsidiary to confirm its target of more than EUR 2.4 billion in ordinary net profit for 2026.

Regulated businesses, led by electricity distribution and generation in non-peninsular territories, now contribute nearly half of Endesa's EBITDA, compared with approximately 40 percent a year earlier. Distribution EBITDA rose 24.8 percent to EUR 1.747 billion, supported by the regulatory framework introduced in January and settlements from previous fiscal years.

The mix also carries a caution for Enel investors. Combined EBITDA from generation and commercialisation grew 3 percent to EUR 2.889 billion, but higher renewable generation did not prevent a lower renewables gross margin because realised power prices fell and solar curtailment increased.

Gross investment increased 19.4 percent to EUR 1.622 billion, including about EUR 900 million for distribution networks, up 42 percent year on year. Electricity distributed rose to 114 terawatt-hours from 109 terawatt-hours, while grid losses improved from 9.5 percent to 9 percent. Endesa generated EUR 3.5 billion of cash flow and ended the period with EUR 11.187 billion of net financial debt.

Enel stock traded at 9.26 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:21 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.54 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30, at 9.31 euros. The real-time quote of Enel stock provides the latest trading indication.

items.t: Waaree Energies Partners with Rajasthan Royals as Main Principal Partner
sum: Waaree Energies Limited has officially announced its partnership with Rajasthan Royals as the Main Principal Partner through regulatory disclosure under SEBI Regulation 30. The partnership features Waaree's logo prominently on the team's official matchday jersey and training kits, bringing together two brands committed to innovation and sustainability with shared vision to inspire positive change through sport.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

The company filed the announcement on March 18, 2026, with both BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited, fulfilling its disclosure obligations under SEBI listing requirements. The revised press release titled "Waaree Energies powers up as the main Principal Partner for Rajasthan Royals" was submitted by Company Secretary Rajesh Ghanshyam Gaur.

As part of the association, Waaree Energies logo will prominently feature on the front of Rajasthan Royals' official matchday jersey and training kits for the season. The partnership brings together two brands aligned in their commitment to innovation and sustainability, with a shared vision to inspire positive change through sport.

Hitesh Doshi, CMD of Waaree, emphasized the cultural significance of cricket in India, stating that the partnership enables the company to take the message of clean energy from industry corridors to the hearts of people across the country. He highlighted that as India advances towards global leadership in clean energy, this movement must extend beyond businesses to become a people's movement.

Alok Chitre, COO of Rajasthan Royals, welcomed Waaree Energies as their Main Principal Partner, noting that the partnership reflects their philosophy of transforming society through cricket and cricket through innovation. He emphasized that Waaree's leadership in driving the global energy transition aligns seamlessly with their commitment to building a forward-looking, purpose-led franchise.
Established in 1990, Waaree Energies operates advanced manufacturing facilities with a total solar PV module capacity of approximately 22.30 GW worldwide and a solar cell capacity of up to 5.40 GW.

items.t: Here's why Waaree Energies share price rose 6% in trade on March 17
sum: The company informed the exchanges that Waaree Solar Americas Inc (WSA), its wholly owned subsidiary, has completed the acquisition of 5,368,551 Series B preferred shares of United Solar Holding Inc

Waaree Energies Share Price: Renewable energy player Waaree Energies witnessed strong investor demand for its shares on Tuesday, March 17, after the company announced an acquisition update. Following the announcement, the company’s share price climbed 5.88 per cent to hit an intra-day high of ₹2,955 per share on the NSE.

The stock, however, trimmed some gains but continued to trade higher on the bourses. At 11:18 AM, it was quoted at ₹2,917 per share, up 4.53 per cent from its previous close of ₹2,790.70 on the NSE. The benchmark Nifty 50, meanwhile, was trading at 23,444, up 36 points or 0.15 per cent.
A combined total of 3.14 million equity shares of Waaree Energies, estimated to be worth ₹920.17 crore, changed hands on the NSE and BSE during the day.
The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹84,011.28 crore on the NSE, as of March 17. The stock has a 52-week range of ₹3,865 to ₹1,863 per share on the NSE.

Earlier, on December 19, 2025, the company had informed the exchanges that Waaree Solar Americas Inc had executed a binding term sheet with United Solar Holding Inc, a Cayman Islands-based company, on December 18, 2025, for subscription of approximately 5,368,551 Series B preferred shares of USH for a purchase price of around $30,000,000, subject to the satisfaction of various conditions required prior to closing, as are customary for transactions of this nature.

items.t: Enel, profit up 18% to 2028 and investments of 53 billion. Renewables, focus on Italia, Spain and the USA
sum: Twenty billion will be allocated to green plants, 26 billion to Networks, 75% in Europe and the rest in Latin America

Enel is gearing up for a new three-year period of growth, both in terms of profitability and shareholder remuneration, and in terms of investments. The board of directors approved the business plan 2026-28, which envisages earnings per share rising by 18% over the three-year period, from an expected EUR 0.69 per share at the end of 2025 to a maximum of EUR 0.82 per share. Meanwhile, the coupon for the 2025 financial year is announced, which will be EUR 0.49 per share compared to a 2024 dividend of EUR 0.47 per share. The plan is to achieve a cumulative Ebitda of 74 billion over the three-year period (which means a pace of around 24 billion per year, compared to 22.9 billion achieved at the end of 2025).

At the same time, the group is preparing to increase investments over the period by around 10 billion to a total amount of 53 billion between 2026 and 2028. Enel announced that it has maintained the targets announced with the previous plan: 15 billion was distributed to shareholders between dividends and planned buybacks. Meanwhile, on 22 February the board of directors approved a new one billion buyback plan, with the purchase of up to 150 million treasury shares. Thanks to the work done in recent years, the group has acquired financial flexibility of 15 billion to increase investments and shareholder remuneration.

About EUR 20 billion will be allocated to renewables, an increase of about EUR 8 billion over the previous plan to add about 15 GW of new renewable capacity, both greenfield (i.e. plants built from scratch) and brownfield (existing plants). The focus will be on geographies characterised by significant growth in electricity demand. Specifically, the group has planned to invest about 50% of its investments in renewables in Europe (mainly Italia and Spain), to be allocated among public auctions, hybridisation and repowering of plants, as well as brownfield opportunities.
